newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-HAYDEN SCORES MAIDEN TON AS AUSTRALIA FORGE AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HAYDEN SCORES MAIDEN TON AS AUSTRALIA FORGE AHEAD.

text.p: Australia's Mark Waugh and opener Matthew Hayden, who scored his maiden test century, plundered 95 runs from a depleted West Indies attack in the morning session of the second day of their fourth test match.
Australia were 234 for two at lunch on Sunday and look set to build a huge lead over the West Indies' dismal first innings total of 130.
Leading the five match series 2-1, Australia now look assured of at least a draw, which would be enough to retain the Frank Worrell trophy they won from the West Indies in the Caribbean in 1995.
Hayden's century in his third test match for Australia was the feature of a morning which began with the West Indies striving for a breakthrough to claw back into the match.
The 25 year old Queenslander (105 not out) struggled early in the session against some accurate fast bowling from captain Courtney Walsh and Ian Bishop.
A nervous Hayden was stuck on his overnight score of 66 for an agonising 43 minutes, a period which included being caught while slashing a wide ball to cover off a no ball from Bishop.
Hayden's first scoring shot of the day, an uppish drive for four through mid-off, only just missed a despairing Walsh at mid-off.
He was lucky to survive again when dropped on 82 off Walsh's bowling in the 14th over of the morning.
Wicketkeeper Junior Murray dived across in front of first slip Brian Lara to catch a Hayden nick, only to put it down in front of an incredulous Lara.
Hayden was let off in similar fashion late on the first day on 58 when Murray decided to leave another nick to Lara, who let it go thinking it was Murray's catch.
Words and glares were exchanged again in the slips this morning after the mix-up. Walsh appeared inconsolable, his eyes to the heavens and his arms outstretched in disbelief.

Hayden then decided to attack and made the West Indies pay for their indiscretions, particularly as Walsh was forced to bring on his inexperienced and often wayward seamers Cameron Cuffy and Patterson Thompson.
Elegant right hander Mark Waugh also punished the two pace bowlers, and was not out at 76 at lunch.
The West Indies had to draft in the two youngsters -- Cuffy and Thompson -- who have only three tests between them, after injuries to Curtly Ambrose and Kenny Benjamin.
Hayden cut decisively backwards of point off Cuffy to bring up his century and Australia's 200 in 267 minutes from 179 balls with 14 fours.

Hayden, who struggled for test selection for the last five years despite hefty scores in domestic cricket, crossed himself and raised his bat in salute to a standing ovation from the crowd of over 20,000 and the dressing room.
